title: Isomorphisms of category-valued sheaves are detected on a covering family of objects
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ (a collection $J(V)$ of covering sieves on each object $V$, satisfying the maximal-sieve, pullback, and transitivity axioms); a sieve is a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition. Use the site and set-sheaf terminology of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal A$ be any category. An $\mathcal A$-valued $J$-sheaf is a functor $F:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal A$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(a,F(-))$ is a sheaf of sets for every $a\in\mathcal A$ (matching families on covering sieves have unique amalgamations). Write $\Sh(J,\mathcal A)$ for their category, with natural transformations as morphisms. Let $(C_i)_{i\in I}$ be a small family of objects such that for every $V\in\mathcal C$ the sieve of arrows $W\to V$ whose domain $W$ admits a morphism to some $C_i$ is in $J(V)$. For $C_i$, the slice category $\mathcal C/C_i$ has arrows $W\to C_i$ as objects and commuting triangles as morphisms. Its induced topology declares a sieve on $W\to C_i$ covering exactly when its underlying arrows to $W$ form a sieve in $J(W)$. Let $r_i:\Sh(J,\mathcal A)\to\Sh(J|_{C_i},\mathcal A)$ be restriction, $(r_i F)(W\to C_i)=F(W)$. If $\varphi:F\to G$ is a morphism of $J$-sheaves and $r_i\varphi$ is an isomorphism for every $i\in I$, then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.
